Inspecteur,\n\nVoici ce que je vous deva:
Inspector,

Here is what I owed you. On the left, the original travel register from 40921, as it entered basement B on 22 October, closed and initialled. On the right, the copy Section 4 sent you.

Read the third line. On the original, it does not exist. The Velmira > Halvek journey of 21 October was added to the copy, after closure, in a different ink, with a stamp dated the 24th.

SEDLAR may well have been at his post that day, as the certificate said. The contradiction you "established" had been prepared for you.

Don't thank me. Burn this note.

K.

Inspector,

We have received your note: you claim that a closed register was "completed" afterwards. The archivist KREMER consults many originals; we know where your document comes from.

The matter is closed. Only one thing is now on file: your name, and the day you called into question a document already ruled on. B.

Inspecteur,\n\nVous posez le bordereau s:
Inspector,

You put the slip on my desk, with my name on it. Yes, it was I who handed you 40921. It had been handed to me as well, already completed. I was not asked to read it, only to pass it down to you.

You wanted to know whom you were dealing with. Now you know — and so do I. Put that document away. Bring it out only on the day it can save you, not today.

R. MAZUR
Inspecteur,\n\nVous venez m'accuser sans:

I will give you some free advice: when you come to accuse me of passing on a forgery, have the forgery in hand, proven. Otherwise it is you they will send down to the basement.

R. MAZUR

File 40921 was put together that same 24.10 and handed to VOSK in person by MAZUR, who had himself received it already "completed" from a higher level. The rest — who held the pen, who gave the instruction — that is no longer archiving. That is your job, not mine.
